context.purpose: Bounded real-valued one-dimensional analysis with numeric CSV publications; use for signals and fitted trends, not arbitrary MATLAB programs.
context.assumptions: Finite real x/y samples; callers own physical units. Frequency is cycles per x unit and phase is radians. Native APIs are described by the public GNU Octave manual; the supported subset is defined by the declarations.
context.constraints: Derivatives, integrals and resampling require strictly increasing x; FFT requires uniform power-of-two sampling. Complex values, missing data, plotting and user functions are unsupported. Sampling, fit and budget constraints on literal and generated tables are checked when planning; nodes that depend on a CSV file are checked at run time, before native launch, because planning never reads files.
context.inspection: Inspect output CSV x/y values and statistics.json; native.json retains intermediates and fit/FFT metadata. Run verify to compare retained native results and publications with independent host arithmetic (relative 2e-8, absolute 2e-9). The embedded derivative example should publish y=[2,2,2].
context.recovery: INVALID_TABLE requires matching x/y lengths and numeric columns. INVALID_SAMPLING (reported at planning for literal data, with the node id as location) requires correcting order, spacing, sample count or smoothing window. A SINGULAR_FIT needs varying x. Repair input, plan again and use a fresh output directory; do not relax verification tolerances to hide disagreement.

workflow.scope: Numeric UTF-8 CSV with named columns; caller supplies units. readCSV consumes table artifacts. No nulls or implicit unit conversion. Verify ordering and hashes before reuse.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure value functions and expressions resolve for every finite analytic visit before native validation.

lifecycle.timeout: One isolated Octave worker receives the runner timeout; input validation precedes launch.
lifecycle.cancellation: Shared process-tree cancellation through native_command.execute; authored input and partial result records remain.
lifecycle.logs: Retain analysis.stdout, analysis.stderr, analysis-submission.json and dispatch metrics.
lifecycle.verification: Recompute every intermediate with independent host arithmetic, compare numeric CSV/statistics, source hashes and artifact membership.

data.scope: Named numeric x/y columns; no implied units.
Two-column ordered numeric output; integration and FFT change interpretation.
Numeric summary and fit/FFT metadata in retained evidence.

inspection.scope: Inspect output CSV columns and selected rows.
inspection.limits: CSV input is bounded to 8 MiB; table pages are bounded by the shared inspection service.
Series views require explicit numeric columns and strictly increasing x.

authoring.reuse: Change the declared dimensions or numeric options using JSON pointer edits; plan the new revision, use a fresh run directory and compare independent expectations.

workflow.scope: Declared artifact receipts, scheduler provenance and explicit handoffs; verify each consumer format.

native-inspection.scope: Inspect retained publications and receipts; no native node inspection hook is advertised.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure value functions and expressions resolve for every finite analytic visit before native validation.

mpi.scope: Only serial execution is qualified; do not request multiple ranks.

reusable-inputs.scope: The registered hook hashes external inputs for scheduler reuse.

time-batches.scope: No finite native time-list batching support in this route.

source-authoring.scope: Edit ordinary JSON through the shared draft source; planning checks the current revision.

property-authoring.scope: Use atomic JSON pointer patches through the shared draft model; node commands apply only to node-shaped routes.

live-editing.scope: Use bounded batch execution; no persistent native editing session is promised.

native-save.scope: Inspect and reuse declared publications; no console native-save extension is advertised for this route.

conversion.scope: Declared exports only; no generic lossless conversion or automatic conversion planning.

cases.scope: Analytic linear-sample derivative; no FFT or arbitrary signal qualification.
